chapter: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
title: Kansas City jam session and Charlie Parker
summary: On the road to Kansas City the overloaded bus was swapped; at the Subway Club jam session set up for Chick, they first saw Charlie Parker, who rode with the band.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: In fact, we travelled so much -- we leaving St. Louis one morning we got on the highway going to Kansas City -- this was the first time I ever played Kansas City with (inaudible) Big Joe Turner.
And they had a little club over there
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
called The Subway Club. All the musicians like the Rhythm Club in New York. All the musicians go down there and cut, you know, have a jam session.
I mean a really -- well they'd go into Kansas City -- we had travelled the road so long on the bus so they stopped us.
The bus was overweight. You know, how they make you weigh the buses -- you got too much weight on the road -- we had to stop and get another bus.
Chick say, "Well, I gotta send all the winter clothes home." We had all this stuff on the bus, we had all these (inaudible) trunks (inaudible).
We been on the road -- you know, we had a lot of stuff on the road. Loaded down -- had been out there (inaudible) with a lot of stuff.
Got another bus and went into Kansas City where we played that big new Kansas City place there -- auditorium.
But they had set up a jam session just for Chick. And we cut -- Chick and I sat in the auditorium trying to duck somebody -- didn't want to
see somebody. So when we got over there, they say, "Come on, we're waiting for you downstairs." We went down there and all these top musicians were down there.
They had this jam session -- (inaudible) drummers about four or five drummers down there. Boy these guys could play // said there (inaudible) Chick (inaudible). They were just entertaining Chick.
Of course, Chick drum some later. He got up later and played something. But that was a jam session just for him. That's when we first saw Charlie Parker, the Bird.
This is 1936.
'36. That's when we saw Charlie Parker. Because Charlie Parker --
What was he doing --
-- went to Oklahoma with us until we called up John Hammond. And John Hammond sent for him to come to New York.
But he was something else.
Playing down there --

He was just down there just gigging.
Jamming.

Just jamming. He told Chick he wanted -- (inaudible). Chick asked could he go with him. Chick say, "Well we're going out to Oklahoma." He say, "I don't care, we'll ride with you." And he travelled with us (inaudible).
